transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Horizon Platform Lead), Ethan Moore (Horizon ML Eng), Sana Riaz (Horizon Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Reviewed latest pilot run with focus on fallback behavior and model pinning.
- Discussed gaps in catalog parity between hosted and dedicated variants and safe rollback triggers.
- Agreed on a 24-hour load test with fallback toggled; to gather cost/latency split and error scenarios.
- Action items assigned for pricing, KMS confirmation, and tabletop drill.

Topics:
- Model selection and pin policy for production cutover
- Emergency hot-swap / fallback playbook and triggers
- Security/compliance items: KMS, audit logs, SOC 2 questions
- Pilot metrics: P50/P95 latency, token cost, failure modes

Transcript:
00:00 Laura Chen: hey everybody, thanks for joining, uh today's the weekly pilot checkpoint, I think we have about 45, 46 minutes on the calendar. Mateo and I will run through the results and then Nina/Ethan/Sana can walk through any concerns.
00:18 Nina Patel: thanks, and yeah just to flag, we've got the exec sync next week so if we can show that the fallback works under load that helps our timeline.
00:28 Mateo Ruiz: cool, we've got the run from Friday — the 6-hour smoke and the 4-hour extended — I'll summarize the latencies and then show the gating rules we prototyped.
00:39 Ethan Moore: quick aside, we saw some token spikes when the prompts were longer, there was a big P95 blip around 2.2 secs, wondering if that's model selection or batching.
00:51 Mateo Ruiz: yeah so two things: one is batching behavior on Redwood host — the continuous batching can sometimes coalesce short bursts; second is model variant differences, we had the same model in hosted and the quantized dedicated build and the dedicated quantized path had slightly faster tail but more variance under mixed sequences.
01:10 Sana Riaz: when you say quantized dedicated, you mean the Dedicated pools, as in our private pool? and we're comfortable with KMS?
01:18 Laura Chen: correct, the Dedicated pool we spun is the reserved GPU pool; I'll note sometimes our docs call it "Redwood Dedi cated" in some transcriptions but it's the same. KMS integration is supported — Mateo will follow up to confirm key rotation and HSM options.
01:36 Mateo Ruiz: right, so for KMS — we have both cloud KMS and HSM connectors; the only caveat we saw was that if you enable client-side envelope encryption it'll add latency to the first token for key unwraps, but that's a one-time per-request cost.
01:53 Nina Patel: do you have an example of the latency impact? exec will ask that.
01:57 Mateo Ruiz: off top, unwrap is usually ~50-120 ms depending on HSM, so P50 unaffected much but it nudges P95. We'll include exact numbers in the run logs.
02:10 Ethan Moore: on model pinning: last week's smoke showed that when we pinned to v1.3 it was stable but v1.4 produced different summaries — sometimes more concise but introduced hallucination on entity linking. Is the fallback policy going to route to previous stable or to a smaller cheaper model?
02:33 Laura Chen: good question. The playbook we've prototyped supports both: soft-fallback to a pinned previous version (v1.3) for safety, and a hard-fallback to a smaller model variant (e.g., semantic-lite) for cost/latency constraints. You can configure thresholds: quality regression triggers, latency SLO breaches, or a circuit breaker for error rate.
02:55 Nina Patel: can we see an example rule?
02:57 Mateo Ruiz: yeah, here's a sample we demoed (link sent in chat: https://redwood.example.com/poc/horizon/rulesheet). rule: if hallucination rate > 0.8% over 1k queries OR P95 > 2.5s for 5m, then pin-back to v1.3 and route 10% to semantic-lite until issue cleared.
03:21 Ethan Moore: the hallucination metric — we need to know how it's computed. We use entity precision/recall on our eval set, but how do you detect it in live?
03:31 Mateo Ruiz: live detection is heuristic — we run a lightweight NER/QA check against our knowledge-base and if the answer conflicts we flag. Not perfect, but it gives a signal for automatic gating. We'll send the heuristics doc.
03:45 Sana Riaz: on auditability, we need immutable logs for any fallback decision. Does Redwood provide those?
03:51 Laura Chen: yes, action logs and routing decisions are stored; we can push them to your SIEM or S3. There's also trace IDs on requests to tie model choice to output. We'll include an example.
04:06 Nina Patel: timeline — if our execs want a demo next week, we need the 24-hour run done and the drill rehearsed. Is that feasible?
04:13 Laura Chen: yes, we can run the 24-hour starting tomorrow, Mateo?
04:15 Mateo Ruiz: yes, I'll kick it off tonight with fallback toggled. We'll produce a sheet with P50/P95, token cost, and error-rate windows.
04:24 Ethan Moore: a nit — the catalog between hosted and dedicated had some naming mismatches so our automation that picks model by name failed in about 6% of calls.
04:33 Mateo Ruiz: hmm, that's a catalog parity issue — we maintain mapping but sometimes shorthand names differ. We can provide a canonical model-id mapping file (we'll attach).
04:44 Nina Patel: good — that mapping will help our infra team. Also, can you outline the emergency hot-swap steps? we want a short checklist we can run with our on-call.
04:54 Laura Chen: sure. High-level: 1) Detect breach (thresholds) -> 2) Evacuate traffic via routing policy to fallback variant -> 3) Pin to last known-good version -> 4) Post-mortem + metrics snapshot. We'll share the one-pager.
05:09 Ethan Moore: and how quick is the hot-swap? do we need to wait for new models to load?
05:13 Mateo Ruiz: swap is config-level routing so switch happens in seconds for new requests; warm KV cache may make first requests slower so we recommend a small percentage ramp for observation before full cutover. If we need instantaneous, we run pre-warmed standby nodes for the fallback — that's an option with Dedicated (cost tradeoff).
05:36 Sana Riaz: on compliance, we need to validate that fallback routing doesn't cause data egress to a different region or external model. We must ensure data residency.
05:45 Laura Chen: absolutely — routing policies can be constrained by region and tenancy; we can restrict fallback to only run within your VPC or Dedicated pool in your region. We'll note that in the runbook.
05:59 Nina Patel: any surprises from logs?
06:02 Mateo Ruiz: two minor ones: one spurious 503 from a transient GPU oom which we throttled and retried automatically, and one mis-happening where a model name mismatch routed to a non-quantized variant causing higher cost.
06:20 Ethan Moore: did you see any error patterns associated with specific prompt lengths?
06:24 Mateo Ruiz: yes, long prompts with lots of context caused KV cache grows and slightly higher tail latencies; we suggest prefix caching for repeated system prompts to reduce cost/latency.
06:38 Nina Patel: what's the suggested pin policy for production? lock at minor version or patch?
06:43 Laura Chen: best practice we've seen is to pin at minor version for the stable window (e.g., v1.3.x) and allow patch auto-rolls for non-breaking fixes; for critical flows pin to exact patch until validation passes. We'll include a policy doc.
06:58 Ethan Moore: if we detect a regression in semantic quality after a patch, we want automatic rollback — is that supported?
07:04 Mateo Ruiz: yes the rollout engine supports automatic rollback based on eval set regressions or production signals; you can set percent traffic thresholds and automated rollback to previous good variant.
07:12 Laura Chen: one thing to call out — the automatic rollback uses the last verified model in your pinned history, not necessarily the immediate previous commit if you have a different verification gate. So maintain the verified history is important.
07:26 Nina Patel: can we mark certain routes as non-rollbackable? for example, billing flows we want manual control only.
07:33 Mateo Ruiz: yes, routes can be tagged as manual-only for rollbacks. We'll show the UI setting.
07:42 Ethan Moore: about the 24-hour load test, what should we measure besides latency and cost?
07:47 Laura Chen: error rate windows, hallucination signal rate, token distribution, KV cache hit ratio, and cold-start penalty. Also trace sample for specific high-latency requests.
08:01 Sana Riaz: for the SOC 2 scope we need to validate audit retention period — what's default?
08:06 Laura Chen: default is 90 days for the hosted logs, but for Dedicated/Private you can retain longer and export to your storage. We'll include options and costs.
08:16 Nina Patel: can you add the retention options in the next email?
08:18 Laura Chen: yes.
08:20 Mateo Ruiz: quick demo share: I'll show the rule sim — sent a link in chat to a short replay: https://redwood.example.com/replays/hz-20260520.
08:35 (screen share) Mateo Ruiz: so here's a simulated spike where we cross the P95 threshold — routing flips 20% to semantic-lite and pins main to v1.3. you can see the trace ids and the routing decision in the logs.
09:05 Ethan Moore: I like the idea of a shadow run where we route duplicates to the new model without affecting production. can we run that during the 24-hour?
09:13 Mateo Ruiz: absolutely — shadowing is low impact and gives a direct comparison. We'll enable shadow for 10% of traffic in the test window.
09:23 Nina Patel: about cost — can you show cost delta table between pinned v1.3 vs v1.4 vs semantic-lite?
09:30 Laura Chen: yes, we'll include a delta per 1k tokens in the spreadsheet; Laura will attach pricing examples.
09:38 (slight crosstalk) Speaker 1: sorry, two quick clarifications on the mapping file and the eval set location.
09:44 Mateo Ruiz: mapping file will be at https://redwood.example.com/poc/horizon/mapping.csv and the eval set is in the shared drive (link in chat).
09:55 Nina Patel: ok, action owner recap?
09:58 Laura Chen: I'll go through the next steps — Mateo run 24-hour, setup shadowing, provide logs; Laura share pricing and runbook; Sana confirm KMS details; Ethan finalize eval prompts. Also schedule tabletop for 5/27.
10:18 Ethan Moore: question — for emergency hot-swap rehearsal, do you recommend a dry-run that forces a rollback?
10:23 Mateo Ruiz: yes a dry-run where you flip routing and monitor rollback is safest; we can orchestrate and be oncall for the first one.
10:31 Sana Riaz: also please include the SIEM webhook example so our security stack can consume the action logs.
10:36 Laura Chen: will do.
10:40 Nina Patel: anything else from Redwood side?
10:43 Mateo Ruiz: nothing major, I'll start the run tonight.
10:46 Laura Chen: thanks everyone — we'll send the recap and artifacts after this call.
